propositions: The reconciler re-attempts the same structurally-impossible inbound Jira→rebar link writes on every pass because failed links never land a LINK event, so the identical record is re-emitted without durable memory of the verdict.

Each of the three deterministic failure shapes (source closed, redundant ancestry, cycle) is classified but only warn-and-continue logged, with no recording mechanism, causing the same 19 doomed writes per pass to repeat indefinitely (~200+ writes/hour).

A durable store of impossible link ADDs, keyed on a digest over the structural inputs the validators read, allows the applier to skip the write on repeated attempts when the digest matches and skip the re-attempt when structural inputs change.

The deciding digest must cover the full parent chain for each endpoint (to capture type-tier ancestry redirects) and the transitive graph for cycle detection, with non-structural edits (comments, titles) excluded so an unchanged structure converges to zero writes.

The impossible_links.json record file must be committed to the tickets branch by _commit_binding_store_snapshot, else records are discarded between fresh CI checkouts and the fix has no effect in production.
